subject: immich-app-immich-28886
note: STANDING sample — chosen once. Grade it blind (relabelled, mixed with live clusters) on every grading day that touches this subject, and record the result with judge_stability.py --calibration. Do not re-draw: a fresh draw confounds sampling with drift.

clusters.summary: Deleting the already-applied ConvertNegativeRatingToNull migration file makes Kysely's unconditional missing-migration check throw 'corrupted migrations' at startup for any database that recorded it, so those servers refuse to boot; keeping the file with a no-op up() avoids it.
Users who ran the deleted migration on main builds already had -1 ratings irreversibly converted to NULL, and the change ships no remediation or changelog note acknowledging it.

BaseSearchSchema.rating still carries .min(1) (and the '-1 no longer valid' history entry), so every derived search DTO rejects rating -1 with HTTP 400 and rejected assets can be set but never searched for, while the search and asset DTO histories now contradict each other.

Moving the rating bounds from .min()/.max() into a .refine() hides them from the JSON-Schema emitter, so UpdateAssetDto/AssetBulkUpdateDto.rating publish minimum/maximum ±9007199254740991 in the OpenAPI spec and generated Dart client instead of a bounded range.
Rating 0 now returns 400 instead of being coerced to null as before the original restriction — a distinct breaking change that no commit message mentions and no test pins.
The refine predicate was suspected of double-reporting on non-integers; 3.5 emits only the int error, though 1e21 emits two issues with no covering test.
Rating field descriptions have drifted across asset.dto.ts, search.dto.ts, and exif.dto.ts, and the new user-facing 'rejected' concept is documented nowhere including the XMP sidecar docs.
SearchRatingsSection's Number.parseInt on the 'null' option yields NaN and options[rating] indexing is off by one for ratings 1-5 (pre-existing, unrelated to -1).

No test asserts that rating -1 is accepted: the controller spec's as-is loop still covers only 1 and 5, and the negative-rating e2e, unit (metadata.service.spec), and round-trip coverage deleted by the original restriction is not restored, so a regression re-restricting -1 would pass CI.
The controller spec's over-max (7) and under-min (-2) rejection cases now assert the same error string, losing diagnostic granularity between the two boundaries (still not a vacuous pass).
The generated Dart client was checked for rejecting rating -1 by range; update_asset_dto.dart does a bare int.parse with no bounds enforcement, so construction cannot fail.

The rating field on UpdateAssetBaseSchema backs AssetBulkUpdateDto as well, but the bulk-update spec block never sends a rating at all, so that DTO's rating validation has no test coverage of any value (pre-existing).

The client-side half of the original restriction is not reverted: the Dart widgets, action/search models and web StarRating.svelte that were changed to stop sending -1 remain as-is, so first-party clients still cannot set a rejection even though the API now accepts it.

The extraction that nulls the rating was checked for re-queuing another sidecar write and thus a self-amplifying job loop; no AssetExtractMetadata -> SidecarWrite edge exists, so the chain terminates after one round trip.

The tree was swept for dangling references to the deleted migration — no manifest, index, seed or doc names it — confirming the breakage lives in the recorded database row rather than in the repository.
